subject: Catalytic uplift credit and annualization checklist
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@noveltech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Catalytic uplift credit and annualization checklist

Hi Emma —

Great talking earlier. Per our conversation, I put together two practical options for handling NovelTech’s mid-contract uplift while keeping your invoice cadence predictable. Attached: uplift-options.xlsx and a short annualize-checklist.docx. High-level: 

Option A — Spread credit (preferred for predictable invoicing)
- 12% uplift applied as an invoice-offset spread equally over the next 6 invoices (monthly).
- Credit shows as line-item: "Uplift Credit (Jul–Dec 2028)" with monthly reduction.
- No expiration aside from being fully consumed on the last amortized invoice.

Option B — Bucket + true-up (preferred if you want a single reconciliation)
- One-time credit applied to next invoice, with a 90-day true-up window to reconcile actual usage.
- If usage > forecast, remainder invoiced pro-rata; if < forecast, residual credit rolls forward for 3 months.

A few notes: 
- We can co-term your subscription to 12/31/2028 and align the credit amortization to end-of-year (no proration surprises).
- For procurement: we’ll provide a short DocuSign amendment and an invoice preview for your AP team.
- I flagged Legal/Finance to limit contract changes to an amendment — no full SOW rewrite.

Next step: which option aligns with NovelTech’s AP preferences — spread monthly offsets or a single credit with a true-up? If you prefer, I’ll loop in Karthik to model the per-invoice numbers.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0197
redwood.com

From: Emma Clarke <emma@noveltech.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Catalytic uplift credit and annualization checklist

Thanks Sean —

Appreciate the clear options. A couple items from our side: 
1) Predictable AP cadence is key — monthly offsets are preferred, but we can only accept line-item credits that appear on our monthly statement (your Option A looks promising).
2) We cannot accept credits that expire mid-contract without explicit renewal language. If you propose amortization, it needs to be tied to an amendment that co-terms to our FY end (12/31/2028).
3) Can you confirm what happens if our usage spikes above forecast in August/September? We need to understand timing on true-ups/invoices so we don’t get hit with a surprise large invoice.

Also copying Liam (procurement) so he can confirm what NovelTech’s AP team will allow on the PO. If you can send a sample invoice preview and the DocuSign amendment link, that will speed things up.

—Emma
Emma Clarke
Head of Platform Integrations, NovelTech
emma@noveltech.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: internal: calibrated proposal for NovelTech — numbers and legal note

Sean/Karthik —

Tweaks based on Emma’s asks: we should lead with Option A (monthly offsets) and include an explicit clause in the amendment: "Credits amortized over invoices X–Y; unused credits roll forward to next 3 invoices; expire thereafter only if co-term is not executed." That addresses the expiration concern.

Quick calc (from uplift-options.xlsx):
- Current ARR baseline for seat & inference units: $1,200,000 annualized
- Proposed uplift ask: +12% (incremental $144,000)
- Agreed credit: 10% of uplift ($14,400) to be amortized over 6 months = $2,400 monthly offset

Operational flow I recommend:
1) We publish a one-page amendment (no SOW changes).
2) DKIM-signed DocuSign packet with amendment + invoice preview PDF attached.
3) Credit applies as line-item, visible to AP, with a short enumerated true-up process (30-day notice before true-up invoice).

I’ll create proposal-v2.pdf with language for Legal. Karthik — can you run a quick model on worst-case invoice exposure if usage spikes 2x for two months? We should be able to show NovelTech the capped exposure.

Monica
Monica Patel
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposal-v2.pdf (pdf)

Emma / Liam —

Thanks — we’re aligned. Quick recap and next steps so AP has a concrete path: 

Recap of agreed approach (Option A — monthly amortized offsets):
- Credit: $14,400 (10% of uplift) applied as a monthly offset of $2,400 across 6 invoices (Jul–Dec 2028).
- Co-term: subscription end date set to 12/31/2028 in the amendment.
- Spike protection: any usage above forecast will be invoiced in the normal cadence; we will cap immediate exposure by allowing a 30-day notice true-up and offer a 2-month grace window with invoice smoothing (Karthik to provide a short "spike exposure" table).

Action items: 
1) Sean: send DocuSign amendment packet (link below) — includes amendment + invoice preview + credit schedule.
2) NovelTech/AP: confirm PO number and whether AP requires invoice net terms changes.
3) Monica: finalize proposal-v2.pdf and ensure Legal has the amendment language about credit roll-forward and expiration.
